taoteching.1.meaning: The opening chapter says the true Way can't be fully captured in words or names. Name it and you've already made it smaller. Approach it without grasping and you glimpse its depth; approach it full of desire and you see only its surface.
taoteching.1.today: Some of the most important things, love, meaning, wisdom, resist definition. Over-defining them can shrink them.
taoteching.1.you: Leave room in your thinking for what can't be measured or specified. Not everything worth building fits in a requirements document.

taoteching.8.meaning: The highest goodness is like water. It benefits everything without competing, and settles in the low places people avoid. So it's close to the Way. Be still of mind, keep good company, govern for order, act when the time is right, and don't strive against others.
taoteching.8.today: Humble, useful, adaptable: water is a model for leadership that serves rather than dominates.
taoteching.8.you: Lead like water this week: take the unglamorous jobs, flow around obstacles, and make things grow without needing credit.

taoteching.9.meaning: Better to stop short than to fill a cup to the brim. A blade sharpened too much won't keep its edge. A hall full of treasure can't be guarded. Wealth and honour that breed arrogance bring their own downfall. When the work is done, step back.
taoteching.9.today: Knowing when enough is enough, and when to step away, is a rare and valuable skill.
taoteching.9.you: When a project succeeds, hand it on and let others own it. Stepping back at the peak is the way of Heaven.

taoteching.11.meaning: Thirty spokes meet at the hub, but it's the empty centre that makes the wheel useful. A pot is useful for its hollow; a room for its space. What's there gives form, but what isn't there gives use.
taoteching.11.today: Empty space, in calendars, designs and minds, is where usefulness lives.
taoteching.11.you: Design slack into your systems and your week. Capacity you haven't filled is what lets you respond.

taoteching.17.meaning: The best rulers are barely known. Next come those people love and praise, then those they fear, and worst, those they despise. The best leaders speak little, and when the work is done, the people say they did it themselves.
taoteching.17.today: The finest leadership makes teams feel capable and self-directed, not dependent.
taoteching.17.you: Measure your leadership by how much your team can do without you. Aim for them to say they did it themselves.

taoteching.22.meaning: The bent becomes straight, the empty becomes full, the worn becomes new. Those who want little get it; those who want much go astray. The sage doesn't show off, so he shines; doesn't boast, so his merit is recognised; doesn't compete, so no one can compete with him.
taoteching.22.today: Self-promotion often backfires. Quiet confidence tends to be noticed and trusted.
taoteching.22.you: In your next review or pitch, let the work speak. Resist listing your achievements; mention the team's.

taoteching.30.meaning: Anyone advising a ruler in harmony with the Way won't use force of arms to dominate. Armies leave thorns and bad harvests behind. A skilled commander strikes a decisive blow and stops, without pressing for total mastery or glorying in it.
taoteching.30.today: Strategists still warn about mission creep and victory disease. Knowing when to stop is part of winning.
taoteching.30.you: In defence and strategy, define what decisive looks like before you start, and stop there. Force breeds its own return.

taoteching.33.meaning: Knowing others is cleverness; knowing yourself is wisdom. Overcoming others is strength; overcoming yourself is true power. Whoever is content is rich. Whoever keeps going has will. Whoever dies but isn't forgotten lives long.
taoteching.33.today: Self-knowledge and self-mastery are harder and more valuable than winning against others.
taoteching.33.you: Pick one internal battle, impatience, perhaps, and put the energy there that you'd usually spend competing.

taoteching.37.meaning: The Way does nothing forced, yet nothing is left undone. If rulers held to it, everything would transform by itself. Simplicity without striving brings stillness, and then things go right of their own accord.
taoteching.37.today: Some systems work best when leaders set conditions and stop intervening. Over-managing breaks things.
taoteching.37.you: Look for a process you keep tinkering with. Set it up well, then step back and let it run.

taoteching.47.meaning: Fame or your life: which is dearer? Your life or wealth: which matters more? Chasing fame and hoarding wealth cost you something greater. Whoever is content avoids disgrace; whoever knows when to stop avoids danger and lives long.
taoteching.47.today: It's easy to trade health, time and relationships for money and status without noticing the price.
taoteching.47.you: Ask honestly what your ambitions are costing your health and family. Decide where you'll stop.

taoteching.61.meaning: Government that seems slack may serve people best; government that meddles in everything disappoints. Misery and happiness hide inside each other; who knows how things will end? Even correction can turn into distortion.
taoteching.61.today: Good and bad fortune often reverse. Heavy-handed control has side effects.
taoteching.61.you: Before adding another rule or control, ask whether it could create the very problem it's meant to fix.

taoteching.66.meaning: Act without forcing, deal with affairs without fuss, treat small things as big, and repay injury with kindness. Tackle hard things while they're easy, and big things while they're small. Every difficulty begins as something easy.
taoteching.66.today: Small problems handled early don't become crises. It's the heart of good maintenance and risk management.
taoteching.66.you: Pick one small issue at work or home you've been ignoring and deal with it today, while it's still easy.

taoteching.67.meaning: What's still is easy to hold; what hasn't shown itself is easy to prevent. Act before things appear; bring order before disorder starts. A huge tree grows from a sprout; a tall tower from a heap of earth; a long journey starts with one step.
taoteching.67.today: Prevention beats cure, and great things are built from small beginnings.
taoteching.67.you: Your Pre-Game Shield lives here: act before trouble shows. And for big goals, just take the first step today.

taoteching.79.meaning: At birth we're soft and supple; at death, stiff and hard. Young plants are tender; dead ones dry and brittle. So rigidity goes with death and softness with life. A strong army doesn't conquer; the strongest tree is the one that gets cut down.
taoteching.79.today: Flexibility and adaptability outlast rigidity, in people, organisations and militaries.
taoteching.79.you: Where have you become rigid, in a plan, an opinion, a habit? Loosening up may be the strongest move.

taoteching.84.meaning: Sincere words aren't pretty; pretty words aren't sincere. The wise don't argue; the argumentative aren't wise. The sage doesn't hoard: the more he gives to others, the more he has.
taoteching.84.today: Polished messaging can mask insincerity. Generosity enriches the giver.
taoteching.84.you: Choose plain, true words over polished ones in your next communication. And give something away this week.

taoteching.51.meaning: Learning means adding something every day. The Way means letting go of something every day, until you act without forcing. Then nothing is left undone. The world is won by not meddling.
taoteching.51.today: Growth sometimes means subtracting: fewer commitments, fewer habits, less noise.
taoteching.51.you: Instead of adding a new goal, remove one thing from your life this week. Swapping the feed for Stoa was a start.
